items.title: D. Mass. vacates DHS fixed-admission / end-of-duration-of-status final rule
items.summary: On 16 November 2026, Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV (D. Mass.) granted plaintiffs’ motion for summary judgment and denied defendants’ in Presidents’ Alliance v. DHS, No. 1:26-cv-13799 (ECF 73). The court VACATED the 17 July 2026 Final Rule (91 Fed. Reg. 44976, FR Doc. 2026-14439) under APA § 706 as arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, and otherwise not in accordance with law, and directed entry of final judgment; ECF 74 dismisses the case (terminated 16 November 2026). The opinion incorporates the 14 September 2026 PI analysis, adds that DHS failed to consider SEVIS enhancements as a less burdensome alternative, and holds the rule’s academic-mobility limits contrary to 8 U.S.C. § 1101(a)(15)(F). The court rejected remand without vacatur, noting the rule never took effect. Duration of status remains the governing framework unless a higher court stays or reverses the judgment or DHS issues a new rule. The First Circuit appeal of the PI (No. 26-2112) was still pending as of the order and as of this scan (CL last known filing still 4 November 2026); no stay of the vacatur was found on the district docket this morning. ICE SEVIS / Study in the States pages still showed the July 17 final-rule banner. Not legal advice.
items.slate_impact: Material for the entire Fall 2027 CS/MBA/MSF international slate (and the separate quant/MFE track): a final merits vacatur, not only the prior nationwide § 705 postponement. Duration of status remains the framework unless stayed or reversed on appeal. MSF and same- or lower-level / joint-degree pathways are expressly in scope of the court’s academic-mobility holding. Not school-specific.
